title: Eight hex digits back into a float
hints: `Int32.of_string ("0x" ^ bits)` is fine: it gives the 32 bits as an `int32`. The wrong step is `Int32.to_float`, which makes a float with the same value as `n`.
The `Int32` module has a function that keeps the bits and changes only what they mean. Its name ends in `_of_bits`.
explain: `Int32.of_string` with a `0x` prefix accepts all 8 hex digits, even with the top bit set, and `Int32.float_of_bits` reads those same 32 bits as an f32. No arithmetic happens, so nothing is rounded: `-0.0`, `nan`, infinities and the smallest subnormal all come back exactly.
